summary:
I built Astronaut Blood Pressure Check-in, a web tool that gives astronauts a fast, plain-language screening check on any mission. An astronaut enters a systolic and diastolic reading in mmHg, picks their mission phase from pre-flight, in-flight, or post-flight and taps Review reading. The tool validates the values, then classifies the single reading into a screening range: severe-high, high (stage 1 or 2), elevated, within range, low, or mixed, and explains in plain words what to do next, including contacting the crew medical officer. An urgent-symptoms warning is shown throughout. It then scans 92 complete study-level blood pressure pairs from real flown-crew research (Lee, 2025, Mendeley Data) which showed 37 high, 15 elevated, 37 within range, 1 severe-high, and 2 low with a searchable reference table by phase, mission, participants, and source study, so any reading can be compared with what crews before them actually recorded. It is a demonstration only, not an official NASA system: it saves and transmits nothing, cannot diagnose, and uses general screening ranges rather than a personal baseline, so the crew medical team always makes the final call. Early, understandable warnings like this keep crews healthier on the ISS, Artemis, and a future Mars transit.

what does it do;

- this BP analyzer checks a user input to check for abnormally high or low Blood pressure readings and learned from .

What are the Benefits it has:

-it's main benefit is to help crew spot and treat BP issues that might be serious and has the advantage of being able to give the crew an early warning system when days or hours away from earth.

The Intended Impact of the Project:

-The intended impact of this project is to help the crew on any space mission to monitor their own health efficiently and effectively

The Tools used in the Creation of this Project:

- The tools I used were VS code with copilot as an assistant , Github for an open source site for the code and Gemini for assistance
